basics.name: HCI fabrication research on joints: Joinery (Zheng, Do and Budd), SpringFit, kyub and Metamaterial Mechanisms (Hasso Plattner Institute HCI lab, Baudisch et al.), plus related Kerf-Canceling Mechanisms and Flaticulation
basics.url: No single home page; a cluster of project pages: Joinery web tool https://clementzheng.github.io/joinery/ (code https://github.com/clementzheng/joinery); SpringFit https://hpi.de/baudisch/projects/springfit.html; kyub https://hpi.de/baudisch/projects/kyub-a-3d-editor-for-modeling-sturdy-laser-cut-objects.html (app at https://kyub.com/); Metamaterial Mechanisms https://hpi.de/baudisch/projects/metamaterial-mechanisms.html (editor https://jfrohnhofen.github.io/metamaterial-mechanisms/, code https://github.com/jfrohnhofen/metamaterial-mechanisms)
basics.resource_type: GitHub repo or dataset / interactive tool (research prototypes with academic papers); not a catalogue in the encyclopedia sense
basics.cost: Free: Joinery web tool, Metamaterial Mechanisms editor and code, HPI author copies of the papers. kyub runs free in the browser with a login option and an anonymous mode [uncertain]. SpringFit: paper and video only; no public download of the tool was found [uncertain]. ACM Digital Library versions may be paywalled
basics.license: Joinery code: MIT (Copyright 2016 clementzheng, LICENSE.md). Metamaterial Mechanisms editor: MIT (Copyright 2016 Johannes Frohnhofen, Alexandra Ion). Flaticulation code is on GitHub (licence not checked) [uncertain]. kyub: closed web app, no licence stated [uncertain]. Project pages are 'Copyright Hasso-Plattner-Institut 2026' and papers are ACM-published, so link to them and do not copy figures
basics.year: Metamaterial Mechanisms UIST 2016 (follow-up 'Understanding Metamaterial Mechanisms', CHI 2019); Joinery web tool (c) 2016, Instructable published 6 Feb 2017, paper at Creativity & Cognition 2017; kyub CHI 2019; SpringFit UIST 2019; Kerf-Canceling Mechanisms UIST 2020; Flaticulation UIST 2022. Pages still online in September 2026 (HPI pages 'Copyright 2026'; CMU Interactive Structures page 'Last update: 21 Sep 2026')
basics.access_barrier: none for the Joinery and metamaterial web editors and HPI project pages; the metamaterial deformation simulation needs a desktop install on Windows (Rhino 5, Grasshopper, Karamba); Flaticulation needs Rhino and Grasshopper on Windows; kyub may need a free login to save [uncertain]
basics.image_license: All rights reserved: figures and photos belong to the authors, HPI or ACM (HPI offers press photos for download); the MIT licences cover code, not the paper figures [uncertain for press-photo terms]
basics.authority_level: academic peer-reviewed (ACM UIST, CHI and Creativity & Cognition papers, mostly from the Hasso Plattner Institute HCI lab (Patrick Baudisch), plus Joinery by Clement Zheng, Ellen Yi-Luen Do and Jim Budd, and Flaticulation by Chiao Fang, Vivian Hsinyueh Chan and Lung-Pan Cheng; Metamaterial Mechanisms was nominated for the UIST 2016 best paper award / honourable mention)

coverage.covers: Clever joints and one-piece mechanisms for laser cutting and 3D printing. Joinery: 9 parametric joint profiles in its code (loop insert, loop insert overlap, loop insert surface, 90-degree finger joint, angled finger joint, hem, tab insert, interlocking, flap) for laser-cut sheets, including thin flexible sheet (0.5 mm defaults) and 3 mm board; the paper describes six joint profiles [uncertain]. SpringFit: replaces press-fit mounts (for buttons, motors, LEDs), finger joints, cross (notch) joints and T-joints with cantilever-spring versions that work on any laser cutter and in plywood or acrylic. kyub: 3D editor that builds strong furniture from 4 mm plywood out of finger-jointed closed boxes ('boxels'), plus dowel joints and a 'supported lengthening joint' with butterfly-like tabs for plates bigger than the cutter bed. Metamaterial Mechanisms: 3D-printed cell grids where 'shear cells' act as hinge arrays, giving one-piece mechanisms: a door latch (turn handle to pull latch), pliers, four-bar linkage, pantograph and a Jansen walker. Related work from the same labs: Kerf-Canceling Mechanisms (wedge-based bearings, sliders and gear pairs that work at any kerf) and Flaticulation (T-pattern laser-cut joints that clutch at set angles, and detent hinges). Roughly 25 distinct joint or mechanism types across the cluster
coverage.organisation: Each project is a separate paper with its own figures, grouped by research problem (fit across machines, strength, parametric generation, compliant mechanisms) rather than by the job the joint does. There is no shared index; you need to know the project names. The papers explain each joint with numbered photo figures, which is clear once you find them
coverage.scope_match: high: these are exactly unusual, clever connection and mechanism TYPES that act as one unit (cantilever-spring press-fit replacements, kerf-independent bearings, one-piece compliant door latch and pliers, detent hinges, interlocking and loop-insert sheet joints), with tested rules. Limits: small number of types, mostly laser cutting (a lower priority for the project) and research-prototype tools
coverage.taxonomy_used: No shared taxonomy. Joinery classifies by joint profile (9 in code: finger, angled finger, loop insert x3, hem, tab insert, interlocking, flap). SpringFit classifies by what the press fit holds: mount (round or non-round), finger joint, cross/notch joint, T-joint (4 classes). Metamaterial Mechanisms builds up from cell types (rigid cell, shear cell) to members and hinges, basic mechanisms (hinge, four-bar), compound mechanisms and simple machines (4 levels). Kerf-Canceling Mechanisms classifies by mechanism: bearing, slider, gear pair
coverage.example_types: cantilever-spring mount (SpringFit spring-loaded press-fit replacement); cantilever-spring finger joint; cantilever-spring cross (notch) joint; cantilever-spring T-joint; constant-stress cantilever spring; loop insert joint (Joinery hook-and-loop sheet joint); hem joint (folded seam); tab insert joint (tab and slot with flap); interlocking joint (flexible interlocking flaps); flap joint; angled finger joint; boxel (finger-jointed closed box module, kyub); supported lengthening joint with butterfly tabs (kyub); boxel dowel joint (poseable push-fit joint); shear cell hinge array (metamaterial living hinge); metamaterial door latch (one-piece rotary-to-linear compliant latch); metamaterial pliers; metamaterial four-bar and pantograph; kerf-canceling bearing (self-similar wedge insert that jams on its axle); kerf-canceling slider and gear pair; Flaticulation articulated-angle T-pattern joint and detent hinge
coverage.making_methods: Laser cutting (Joinery, SpringFit, kyub, Kerf-Canceling Mechanisms, Flaticulation) in plywood, acrylic, card and thin sheet; FDM 3D printing in flexible TPU (NinjaFlex, SemiFlex) and laser-cut rubber foam for Metamaterial Mechanisms
coverage.item_count: About 25 joint and mechanism types across 6 projects: Joinery 9 joint profiles (code); SpringFit 4 converted types; kyub 3 joint kinds (finger-jointed boxel, dowel, lengthening joint); Metamaterial Mechanisms about 6 demo mechanisms (hinge, four-bar, door latch, pliers, pantograph, Jansen walker); Kerf-Canceling 3 (bearing, slider, gear pair); Flaticulation 2 (articulated joint, detent hinge)
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: Compliant: yes, strongly (metamaterial shear-cell hinge arrays; SpringFit cantilever springs; Joinery interlocking and loop-insert flexible joints). Print-in-place / no assembly: yes, metamaterial mechanisms are single printed parts. Self-locking / hand-release: partly, the metamaterial door latch is a spring-returned latch opened by turning the handle; SpringFit mounts hold parts by spring force and let them be removed. Indexing/detent: yes, Flaticulation detent hinges and set-angle clutching joints. Torque-limiting, one-way/ratchet, over-centre: none found. Gear trains: only kerf-canceling gear pairs (and the kyub/Jansen walker needs a separate axle); no gearboxes. Powered connectors: none (SpringFit only mounts motors and LEDs). Adhesives: none; kyub and SpringFit are designed to hold without glue (kyub test objects were press fit, not glued)
coverage.entry_structure: Per project: project page with summary, captioned figures, publication details, PDF, demo video and (for some) code and a live tool. Per joint inside a paper: name, photo figure, how it works, design parameters (length, thickness, deflection, angle), evaluation. The Joinery tool shows each joint profile's parameters (material thickness, finger width, hook count, grip, tolerance) as editable fields
coverage.audience_level: research (HCI and digital fabrication researchers), with tools aimed at novice designers and hobbyist makers

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: the project pages explain the problem in plain language with good photos (e.g. SpringFit's 'a cantilever spring is simply a long thin piece of material that pushes against the object to be held'), and Joinery has a step-by-step Instructable; but the papers are academic, the tools are research prototypes with limited support, and nothing is organised for someone looking for 'a joint that does X'
usefulness.has_images: yes: high-quality photos and step-by-step figures of each joint and mechanism in the papers and project pages (e.g. SpringFit spring finger, cross and T-joints; the metamaterial door latch with its cell grid)
usefulness.has_animations: yes: demo videos on YouTube and HPI for SpringFit, kyub, Metamaterial Mechanisms (75.6 MB video), Kerf-Canceling Mechanisms and Flaticulation; interactive 3D editors (metamaterial editor with stiffness and force simulation; kyub 3D editor; Joinery 2D joint editor)
usefulness.gaps: Not a catalogue: only about 25 types, spread across separate papers with no common index or naming; laser cutting dominates, with little for FDM printing in rigid plastics; no ratchets, torque limiters, over-centre latches, gearboxes, powered latches or adhesives; tools are research prototypes (metamaterial simulation needs Windows, Rhino 5 and Karamba; SpringFit tool not publicly downloadable [uncertain]); the HPI Thingiverse collection link for metamaterial models returned 404 when opened
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes for project-level links: stable HPI project URLs (e.g. https://hpi.de/baudisch/projects/springfit.html for cantilever-spring joints, https://hpi.de/baudisch/projects/metamaterial-mechanisms.html for the one-piece door latch, https://hpi.de/baudisch/projects/kerf-canceling-mechanisms.html for kerf-proof bearings) and DOIs (e.g. https://doi.org/10.1145/3332165.3347930). No per-joint pages
usefulness.reusable_data: Code is reusable: Joinery (MIT, joint profiles and default parameters in js/joints.js), Metamaterial Mechanisms editor (MIT, JavaScript voxel editor plus Grasshopper simulation, STL export via OpenJSCAD). The list of joint types is facts and can be reused with citation; paper text and figures are ACM/HPI copyright. No structured dataset
usefulness.maintained: Archived research outputs: the tools are no longer developed (Joinery 2016-2017, metamaterial editor 2016, marked 'not a product, but a research prototype' with limited support), but project pages were online in September 2026 and kyub.com still serves its web app. The Thingiverse collection for metamaterial models returned 404
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) Explain why press fits fail (kerf, material stiffness, printer tolerance) and offer a spring-based alternative; the same idea maps directly to 3D-printed snap fits and clearances. (2) A 'robust to machine differences' flag for each entry (does it still work if your printer or cutter is a bit off?). (3) Show a joint as a problem, a failure photo and a fixed version (SpringFit's a/b/c figures). (4) Build mechanisms up from cells: rigid part, hinge, basic mechanism, compound mechanism, as a simple ladder for explaining compliant mechanisms to beginners. (5) The one-piece door latch as a flagship example of a compliant latch. (6) Joinery's idea of letting the user pick joints per edge and exporting a ready cut file could inspire a 'try this joint' generator link
usefulness.design_rules_given: Yes, some: SpringFit halving spring length or doubling its thickness makes it 8x stiffer; a longer, thicker spring of equal stiffness took 7.5x more variation (up to 1.5 mm); typical kerf variation 0.1 mm at 10 N; the two test cutters differed in kerf by 0.12 vs 0.20 mm; springs use a constant-stress cantilever model. kyub: a single finger-jointed boxel in 4 mm 3-layer plywood withstood over 500 kg; plates up to A2 (60 x 40 cm). Metamaterial Mechanisms: best in flexible TPU (NinjaFlex, SemiFlex), better than PLA; laser-cut versions best in rubber foam; the printed Jansen walker survived about 5,000 cycles at about 120 rpm without visible fatigue. Joinery defaults: finger width 8 mm for 3 mm board, interlocking tolerance 0.1 mm
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: Yes: Joinery (web, parametric joints applied to your SVG edges), SpringFit (converts existing SVG cutting plans), kyub (3D web editor that unfolds to SVG plates with kerf correction), Metamaterial Mechanisms editor (voxel/cell editor exporting STL), Kerf-Canceler (finds bearings, sliders and gear pairs in cutting plans and swaps in kerf-canceling versions) and Flaticulation (Rhino/Grasshopper plug-in that unfolds 3D models and adds articulated joints or detent hinges)
usefulness.file_formats: SVG (Joinery, SpringFit, kyub export); STL (metamaterial editor); Grasshopper .gh files (Flaticulation, metamaterial simulation); PDF papers; MP4 and YouTube videos
usefulness.terminology_value: medium: good source for research names of newer types (cantilever-based mounts and joints, metamaterial mechanism, shear cell, hinge array, boxel, kerf-canceling bearing, articulated-angle joint, detent hinge) and for aliases such as notch joint = cross joint = slotted joint = edge lap joint (kyub paper); not a general authority for traditional names
usefulness.decision_support: None as a selector. Joinery offers a joint-profile menu with editable parameters; SpringFit automatically classifies each press fit (mount, finger, cross, T) and picks spring sizes; kyub's paper compares construction methods (notch joints vs closed boxes) by strength
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Builds on earlier HCI fabrication work (FlatFitFab, SketchChair, Platener, CutCAD). SpringFit cites kyub and Joinery as related tools. Metamaterial Mechanisms overlaps with BYU compliant mechanism research (living hinges, four-bars) and with Ion et al.'s 'Understanding Metamaterial Mechanisms' (CHI 2019, automatic design from motion paths). Joinery and kyub overlap with Boxes.py finger joints and living hinges (count finger joints once)
